item.title: Investigation launched into Civic House electrical explosion that injured two
item.description: An Occupational Health and Safety investigation has been launched into the electrical explosion at Civic House in Suva that left two children with severe burns. The Ministry of Employment, Productivity and Workplace Relations has also issued a Prohibition Notice to the Suva City Council, as owner of the building, following preliminary investigations into Wednesday afternoon’s incident.
item.content:encoded:
An Occupational Health and Safety investigation has been launched into the electrical explosion at Civic House in Suva that left two children with severe burns.

The Ministry of Employment, Productivity and Workplace Relations has also issued a Prohibition Notice to the Suva City Council, as owner of the building, following preliminary investigations into Wednesday afternoon’s incident.

The Ministry said preliminary findings indicate an electrical fault occurred at about 3.20pm inside the ground-floor Main Switchboard Room.

Minister for Employment Agni Deo Singh said preliminary OHS findings had identified thermal damage to some electrical components within the switchboard.

However, the precise cause of the electrical fault and the circumstances leading to the incident remain under investigation.

However, Police said the two children, aged six and 13, would normally wait for their mother at their aunt’s office after school.

According to Police, the children were playing hide-and-seek when one entered the switchboard room to hide.

Police said when the second child opened the door while looking for the other, electrical equipment was accidentally touched, triggering the explosion.

Both children suffered severe electrical flash burns and remain under observation at the Colonial War Memorial Hospital.

Following the incident, OHS officials ordered the affected switchboard to be isolated and locked out, with access restricted to authorised repair and inspection personnel.

The Ministry has recommended that electricity not be restored until the installation undergoes a comprehensive inspection and receives technical clearance from the relevant authorities, including licensed electrical contractors and Energy Fiji Limited.

Safety arrangements surrounding electrical rooms within the building are also being examined, with additional measures to be considered to strengthen safety and minimise future risks.

“The safety of workers, visitors and members of the public must always come first,” Singh said.

“Where there are serious risks, those responsible for workplaces have a duty to ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place and are functioning effectively.”

The investigation is expected to establish the cause of the electrical fault and the circumstances that allowed the children to gain access to the switchboard room.

item.title: Rokotunidau to Appear in High Court Over Bail
item.description: SAIMONI Rokotunidau, who is facing an attempted murder charge, will appear in the High Court in Suva on September 24 for a hearing on whether his bail should be revoked. Mr Rokotunidau is accused of attempting to murder Police Constable Senoveva Tikoduadua, who was allegedly struck by a vehicle while manning a police checkpoint in Laqere, Nasinu, in April.
item.content:encoded:
SAIMONI Rokotunidau, who is facing an attempted murder charge, will appear in the High Court in Suva on September 24 for a hearing on whether his bail should be revoked.

Mr Rokotunidau is accused of attempting to murder Police Constable Senoveva Tikoduadua, who was allegedly struck by a vehicle while manning a police checkpoint in Laqere, Nasinu, in April.

He also faces a charge of unlawful possession of 0.21 grams of methamphetamine.

Mr Rokotunidau pleaded not guilty to both charges before Justice Dane Tuiqereqere today.

His lawyer Jerry Dinati has been given until September 17 to file an affidavit explaining why Mr Rokotunidau failed to attend court on July 29.

The State has been given until September 22 to file its response.

Mr Rokotunidau was arrested on the morning of August 12 at a residence along Nasinu Road following the issuance of a bench warrant.

The accused is alleged to have been involved in the incident in which Constable Tikoduadua was struck by a vehicle.

Constable Tikoduadua is the daughter of Defence and Veterans Affairs Minister Pio Tikoduadua.

Senior Prosecutor Simione Seruvatu appeared for the State, while Mr Dinati appeared for Rokotunidau.

item.title: Bench warrant cancelled after Isaia Ledua arrest
item.description: A bench warrant issued for Isaia Ledua after he failed to appear in the High Court in Suva today was cancelled after his lawyer told the court he had been arrested. Mr Ledua’s case, involving an alleged break-in at the Queen Elizabeth Barracks armoury, was called before Justice Dane Tuiqereqere at 9.30 am today.
item.content:encoded:
A bench warrant issued for Isaia Ledua after he failed to appear in the High Court in Suva today was cancelled after his lawyer told the court he had been arrested.

Mr Ledua’s case, involving an alleged break-in at the Queen Elizabeth Barracks armoury, was called before Justice Dane Tuiqereqere at 9.30 am today.

Mr Ledua was not present when the matter was called, prompting the judge to issue a bench warrant.

Justice Tuiqereqere had earlier reminded Mr Ledua to appear in court at the scheduled time.

However, his lawyer Jerry Dinati later appeared before the same judge and informed the court that Mr Ledua was arrested last night and was being held at Nabua Police Station.

Justice Tuiqereqere subsequently cancelled the bench warrant.

Senior Prosecutor Simione Seruvatu appeared for the State.

The judge adjourned the matter to September 17.

item.title: 14-year prison term for former cop in cousin abuse case
item.description: A former police officer has been sentenced to 14 years and nine months in prison for sexually violating his cousin over three years. The 44-year-old married father-of- three was sentenced by Justice Dane Tuiqereqere in the High Court in Suva today on three counts of rape and four counts of sexual assault.
item.content:encoded:
A former police officer has been sentenced to 14 years and nine months in prison for sexually violating his cousin over three years.

The 44-year-old married father-of- three was sentenced by Justice Dane Tuiqereqere in the High Court in Suva today on three counts of rape and four counts of sexual assault.

The offending occurred between 2019 and 2021 when the victim was 13 years old.

In sentencing the man, Justice Tuiqereqere said he had taken advantage of the victim and sexually exploited her.

The defence had asked the court to balance justice with mercy.

However, the court noted the breach of trust, the 24-year age gap between the offender and victim and other aggravating factors.

Justice Tuiqereqere said the victim had suffered considerably as a result of the offending, including anxiety, loss of trust and ongoing psychological harm.

The judge said there was no doubt the psychological damage caused by the offending had a lasting impact on the victim’s life.

The man will be eligible for parole after serving 10 years and nine months of his head sentence.

The man was represented by Lawyer Joji Cakau, while the State was represented by Katarina Dugan.

item.title: Judicial review for firm
item.description: THE High Court has questioned why a key letter recommending the registration of Goundar Fast Ferry, MV Captain Inoke, was not disclosed to the court in a ruling granting the company leave to challenge the continued delay through judicial review. Justice Anjala Wati said the respondents had failed to bring to the court’s attention a September 1, 2025, letter from the Maritime Safety Authority of Fi
item.content:encoded:
THE High Court has questioned why a key letter recommending the registration of Goundar Fast Ferry, MV Captain Inoke, was not disclosed to the court in a ruling granting the company leave to challenge the continued delay through judicial review.

Justice Anjala Wati said the respondents had failed to bring to the court’s attention a September 1, 2025, letter from the Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji’s (MSAF) then CEO to the Minister for Public Works, Transport and Meteorological Services, recommending registration of the vessel.

The respondents in the case are MSAF, the minister, the Prime Minister and the Attorney-General.

Justice Wati said the letter was significant because it followed earlier MSAF correspondences which initially recommended against registration, but now stated that the vessel was seaworthy and fit to operate as a ferry, subject to safety, technical and operational conditions.

She questioned why the document, which was in the respondents’ possession, had not been disclosed and rejected the explanation that it was an internal or confidential document.

The letter, she said, concerned GFF and its right to have the vessel registered.

Justice Wati found there was an arguable case that the minister had failed to perform his statutory duties by not acting on the then CEO’s recommendation for more than six months.

She said the Constitution required executive and administrative action to be lawful, rational, proportionate, procedurally fair, and reasonably prompt.

The case involves the MV Captain Inoke, a second-hand vessel more than 20 years old which GFF purchased from South Korea and brought to Fiji in January 2025.

Earlier MSAF correspondence had identified outstanding dry-dock, hull survey and compass adjustment requirements.

However, the September 1 letter stated that MSAF had conducted five safety and technical assessments and a sea trial, with 38 of 39 identified defects addressed.

Justice Wati also rejected the respondents’ argument that the vessel had been illegally imported, noting that MSAF had accepted its arrival and subsequently engaged with GFF over the defects.

GFF was granted 28 days to file its judicial review proceedings and awarded $3500 in costs, payable within 14 days.

item.title: New Sydney hub | Direct flights to bridge gap for tourism and diaspora
item.description: NATIONAL carrier Fiji Airways has secured a major competitive edge in the trans-Tasman market by becoming the first international airline to announce direct services to the new Western Sydney International Airport. Scheduled to start operations with the modern Boeing 737 MAX 8 in March next year with three flights a week – Mondays, Fridays and Sundays, the new service will give Fijians an addition
item.content:encoded:
NATIONAL carrier Fiji Airways has secured a major competitive edge in the trans-Tasman market by becoming the first international airline to announce direct services to the new Western Sydney International Airport.

Scheduled to start operations with the modern Boeing 737 MAX 8 in March next year with three flights a week – Mondays, Fridays and Sundays, the new service will give Fijians an additional direct connection between the two countries, and also drive more tourism to Fiji.

Fiji Airways managing director and CEO Paul Scurrah said the new route would add more than 53,000 seats annually between the two destinations.

He said Fiji had just broken the one million visitor mark for a 12-month period for the first time in its history, with the new destination also posting its highest-ever monthly arrivals in July.

That, he said emphasised the strength of the demand and that the new route was a natural next step for the airline.

“It is one of the fastest-growing regions in New South Wales, and a direct route there means easier, more affordable access for Australians looking to holiday in Fiji, which means more visitors, more jobs and more opportunities for our tourism industry,” Mr Scurrah said.

“It’s also home to one of the largest Fijian communities outside Fiji, so this route is about more than just tourism – it’s about making it easier for our people to stay connected to family and friends, and for Fiji to keep growing as a destination the world wants to visit.”

Australia is Fiji’s top tourist source market, and the new service further strengthens connectivity, and created new opportunities for tourism, trade and business travel, he said.

“We’re excited to have Fiji Airways join Western Sydney International as the countdown continues to welcome our inaugural passengers in less than 60 days’ time,” Western Sydney Airport chief executive officer Simon Hickey said.

“Western Sydney is one of the most diverse and rapidly growing regions in the nation, which includes more than 70 per cent of our global city’s Fijian population.

“We’re delighted to be delivering a new, seamless service for them to connect with family and friends, while also giving tourists more choice and flexibility to visit Fiji and explore everything the warm, welcoming leisure destination has to offer.”

Introductory fares are already on ahead of the inaugural service on Friday, March 19, 2027.

item.title: Mill efficiencies deliver 15% boost to sugar production
item.description: A sharp turnaround in mill operations delivered a big win for Fiji’s sugar industry, with sugar production surging by 15.6 per cent as of late August this year. The Reserve Bank of Fiji (RBF) had revealed the sector’s positive trajectory in its August economic review, highlighting a major leap in output that directly affects the livelihoods of thousands of farming families across the Western and N
item.content:encoded:
A sharp turnaround in mill operations delivered a big win for Fiji’s sugar industry, with sugar production surging by 15.6 per cent as of late August this year.

The Reserve Bank of Fiji (RBF) had revealed the sector’s positive trajectory in its August economic review, highlighting a major leap in output that directly affects the livelihoods of thousands of farming families across the Western and Northern divisions.

While the actual volume of cane crushed rose by a modest 2.8 per cent, the total volume of sugar extracted climbed significantly higher.

“Compared with the same period last year, both cane crushed and sugar production rose by 2.8 per cent and 15.6 per cent, respectively, as at August 24, attributed to improved operational performance across all mills and higher sugar extraction rates,” the central bank stated.

The RBF stated other sectoral performances were also generally positive during the review period.

Electricity production, it stated expanded by 4.8 per cent in the year to July, led by growth in Energy Fiji Ltd’s customer base (1.7 per cent) and higher non-renewable energy generation, which more than offset lower renewable energy output resulting from adverse weather conditions.

Over the same period, total gold production also increased by 6.2 per cent, as strong growth in gold concentrate output (58.8 per cent) more than compensated for the decline in gold doré production (-21.8 per cent).

Similarly, mineral water output expanded by 4.2 per cent cumulative to July, consistent with scheduled manufacturing plans and a recovery from the softer output in the corresponding period of 2025 following tariff-related disruptions.

“In contrast, performance in the forestry sector was weaker as mahogany logs (-25.9 per cent), woodchips (-11.2 per cent), and sawn timber (-47.2 per cent) production fell, largely impacted by unfavourable weather conditions,” the central bank stated.

However, it noted pinewood output grew by 3.4 per cent, supported by a higher supply of sawlogs.

Sugar cane trucks line up outside the FSC Rarawai mill in Ba. Picture: REINAL CHAND

item.title: Teacher cops suspended term for slapping student
item.description: A TEACHER who slapped a Class 8 student several times in front of his peers has had his five-month prison sentence suspended for two years. Magistrate Timoci Qalinauci recently convicted and sentenced the teacher for one count of assault.
item.content:encoded:
A TEACHER who slapped a Class 8 student several times in front of his peers has had his five-month prison sentence suspended for two years.

Magistrate Timoci Qalinauci recently convicted and sentenced the teacher for one count of assault.

The court was told the teacher slapped the student several times in the presence of his school mates on one occasion in 2019.

Magistrate Qalinauci said the teacher, who has more than 18 years of teaching experience, had authority over the child and had breached the trust placed in him as a teacher, noting the assault embarrassed the student in front of his peers.

“You must learn to control your anger,” the magistrate told the teacher while passing sentence.

“I am sure there are alternative ways that you can teach; mould a student to be productive inside and outside of the classroom.”

He warned the teacher that committing another offence during the suspension period could result in the activation of the suspended sentence.
